observations.summary: The accuracy of the Cash-in-Bank (CIB) accounts balance as of December 31, 2023, amounting to P9.237 billion could not be established due to: 1) unreconciled variance of P106.634 million between books balances and the result of bank confirmations, and 2) accumulated unadjusted book reconciling items for several years totaling P182.123 million, mainly due to lapses in the preparation and submission of Bank Reconciliation Statements (BRS) contrary to Section 74 of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1445. Thus, affected the fair presentation of the Financial Statement (FS).

recommendations.recommendation: We recommended and Management agreed that the City Accountant (OCAT) and City Treasury Office (CTO): Reconcile the variances between the balances per bank confirmations and book balance, and accordingly effect the necessary adjustments to reflect correct ending balances of CIB accounts;
recommendations.status_note: Reiterated in Part II, Observation No. 1, Page 78
recommendations.management_action: The OCAT submitted the Bank Reconciliation Statements (BRS) for the CIB accounts affected.
recommendations.reason: Although the OCAT submitted the BRS, the book balances of the CIB accounts remain unadjusted.
recommendations.citation: CY 2024 AAR, Part III, CY 2023 Observation No. 1, pp. 178-179

recommendations.recommendation: We recommended and Management agreed that the City Accountant (OCAT) and City Treasury Office (CTO): Cause the timely preparation and submission of monthly BRS for each bank account pursuant to Section 74 of PD No. 1445; and
recommendations.management_action: The OCAT has submitted the BRS.
recommendations.citation: CY 2024 AAR, Part III, CY 2023 Observation No. 1, pp. 178-179

recommendations.recommendation: We recommended and Management agreed that the City Accountant (OCAT) and City Treasury Office (CTO): Formulate a document tracking system to establish accountability for records to provide an effective internal control tool for documentation and recording of the City’s transactions.
recommendations.management_action: The OCAT and CTO are currently implementing a document tracking system that will ensure the proper and timely recording of the financial transactions of the City.
recommendations.citation: CY 2024 AAR, Part III, CY 2023 Observation No. 1, pp. 178-179

observations.summary: The accuracy, completeness, and reliability of the year-end balance of Accounts Payable (AP) amounting to P4.577 billion could not be determined due to net understatement variance of P525.085 million from confirmation results with contractors/suppliers as against balances per books contrary to Paragraph 27 of International Public Sector Accounting Standard (IPSAS) 1. Thus, affecting the fair presentation of the FS.

recommendations.recommendation: We recommended that Management direct: The OCAT to: Identify the causes of variances between recorded accounts payable and the contractors/ suppliers’ confirmed balances and reconcile the same;
recommendations.management_action: The OCAT already undertaken actions to properly account the payables per Supplier. The amount of the variance is already recorded through JEV No. 100-24-04-06 dated June 15, 2024.
recommendations.citation: CY 2024 AAR, Part III, CY 2023 Observation No. 2, pp. 179-180

recommendations.recommendation: We recommended that Management direct: The OCAT to: Coordinate with the City General Services Office (CGSO) as to status of deliveries of goods and services and recognize the corresponding liability if no payment had been made; and
recommendations.management_action: The OCAT is already in close coordination with CGSO regarding the status of deliveries of goods and services procured by the City for recording purposes.
recommendations.citation: CY 2024 AAR, Part III, CY 2023 Observation No. 2, pp. 179-180

recommendations.recommendation: We recommended that Management direct: The OCAT to: Maintain a separate subsidiary ledger (SL) for each contractor/ supplier for proper monitoring of each outstanding payable and status of accounts.
recommendations.management_action: The OCAT has already undertaken actions to properly account for the payables per Supplier.
recommendations.citation: CY 2024 AAR, Part III, CY 2023 Observation No. 2, pp. 179-180

recommendations.recommendation: We recommended that Management direct: The OCAT to: The CGSO to promptly inform the OCAT of deliveries of procured goods and services and furnish the latter with required documents to support the timely recording of transactions.
recommendations.management_action: The OCAT is already in close coordination with CGSO regarding the status of deliveries of goods and services procured by the City for recording purposes.
recommendations.citation: CY 2024 AAR, Part III, CY 2023 Observation No. 2, pp. 179-180

observations.summary: Insufficient imposition of Real Property Tax (RPT) and Special Education Tax (SET) by the City due to: a) Misplaced application of the Assessment Levels (ALs) prescribed under Section 12 of Ordinance No. 8331, s. 2013; and b) Omission of 1,130 Real Property Units (RPUs) in the Assessment Rolls (AR) contrary to Section 2, Chapter II, Manual on Real Property Appraisal and Assessment Operations (MRPAAO), thereby diminishing the City’s earnings to be utilized to finance its programs/projects/activities (PPAs).

recommendations.recommendation: We recommended and the Management agreed that: The Office of the City Assessor – Ensure that Assessment Levels and Assessed Values are accurately computed and provided;
recommendations.management_action: The City Assessor Office has adjusted the assessment levels of the purposes of proper RPT and SET imposition of the identified RPUs.
recommendations.citation: CY 2024 AAR, Part III, CY 2023 Observation No. 3, pp. 180-182

recommendations.recommendation: We recommended and the Management agreed that: Submit to the Auditor’s Office the updated copies of Tax Declaration as proof of corrections/updates made to the 452 RPUs; and
recommendations.management_action: The City Assessor’s Office submitted updated Tax Declarations for audit.
recommendations.citation: CY 2024 AAR, Part III, CY 2023 Observation No. 3, pp. 180-182

recommendations.recommendation: We recommended and the Management agreed that: Appraise and assess the RPUs not included in the Assessment Roll and submit copies of tax declaration as proof appraisal and assessment;
recommendations.management_action: The City Assessor Office has reviewed the identified RPUs and included in the Assessment Roll.
recommendations.citation: CY 2024 AAR, Part III, CY 2023 Observation No. 3, pp. 180-182

recommendations.recommendation: We recommended and the Management agreed that: Review other tax maps not included in the sample to ensure that RPUs inscribed therein are included in the AR;
recommendations.management_action: The City Assessor has reviewed the other tax maps.
recommendations.citation: CY 2024 AAR, Part III, CY 2023 Observation No. 3, pp. 180-182

recommendations.recommendation: We recommended and the Management agreed that: Henceforth, ascertain that RPUs in the tax maps are included in the AR; and
recommendations.management_action: The City Assessor has reviewed the other tax maps.
recommendations.citation: CY 2024 AAR, Part III, CY 2023 Observation No. 3, pp. 180-182

recommendations.recommendation: We recommended and the Management agreed that: The CTO charge and collect from taxpayers the amount of P3,336,539.51 that were under imposed in CY 2023 due to erroneous application of the Assessment Level, and henceforth, ensure that correct amount of taxes is imposed/collected.
recommendations.management_action: The City Treasury imposed the under-assessed tax for those taxpayers that paid their RPT on time.
recommendations.citation: CY 2024 AAR, Part III, CY 2023 Observation No. 3, pp. 180-182

observations.summary: Out of 222 Gender and Development (GAD) PPAs, 22 were unimplemented and 84 were not reported in the GAD Accomplishment Report (AR) or have no status contrary to Republic Act (RA) No. 9710. Thus, the City’s objective of ensuring awareness and sustaining support for gender and development, women’s empowerment and response to gender issues were not fully realized.

recommendations.recommendation: We recommended that Management direct the GAD Focal Point System (GFPS) to: Regularly monitor and evaluate the utilization of the GAD Plan and Budget (GPB) to ensure that PPAs are fully implemented as planned and challenges that cause non-implementation, if any, are identified and addressed;
recommendations.management_action: The GFPS has regularly monitoring and evaluating the utilization of the GAD Fund for the implementation of CY 2024 PPAs. Also, they directed the GAD Focal Persons to carry over the unimplemented 2023 PPAs to the 2024 GAD PPAs.
recommendations.citation: CY 2024 AAR, Part III, CY 2023 Observation No. 4, pp. 182-183

recommendations.recommendation: We recommended that Management direct the GAD Focal Point System (GFPS) to: Ensure that only PPAs listed in the approved GPB will be charged against the GAD Fund; and
recommendations.management_action: -do-
recommendations.citation: CY 2024 AAR, Part III, CY 2023 Observation No. 4, pp. 182-183

recommendations.recommendation: We recommended that Management direct the GAD Focal Point System (GFPS) to: Comply with the provisions of the JMCs discussed and RA No. 9710 and its IRR.
recommendations.management_action: -do-
recommendations.citation: CY 2024 AAR, Part III, CY 2023 Observation No. 4, pp. 182-183

observations.summary: A total of P472.416 million withheld for CY 2023 remittances to the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR), Government Service Insurance System (GSIS), Pag-IBIG and PhilHealth have not been remitted by the City contrary to existing rules and regulations.

recommendations.recommendation: We recommended and Management agreed to ensure prompt and full remittance of all withholding taxes, contributions, premium payments, loan amortization and other amounts due to the BIR, GSIS, Pag-IBIG and PhilHealth pursuant to the above-mentioned regulations.
recommendations.status_note: Reiterated in Part II, Observation No. 14, Page 130
recommendations.management_action: The OCAT, in coordination with the CTO, is continuously remitting the remaining unremitted amount to date.
recommendations.reason: Issues related to employees' details and information (clarificatory items) for GSIS. On the other hand, the amount payable to BIR reflects the withholding taxes related to unpaid amounts payable to different suppliers.
recommendations.citation: CY 2024 AAR, Part III, CY 2023 Observation No. 5, p. 183

observations.summary: The City was unable to identify and appropriate various PPAs for Local Climate Change Action Plan (LCCAP) in CY 2023, which is not inconsonance with Section 14 of RA No. 9729, otherwise known as the Climate Change Act of 2009, as amended.

recommendations.recommendation: We recommended and Management agreed to: Promptly create the City’s LCCAP Core Team in accordance with Paragraph 3.1.1 of Department of the Interior and Local Government -Memorandum Circular (DILG-MC) No. 2014-135 and Section 7 of the City’s LCCAP to facilitate the proper planning, prioritization, funding, implementation and monitoring/assessment of proposed climate change PPAs; and
recommendations.management_action: The Management is currently in the process of creating the Core Team. The necessary documents will be submitted to COA once finalized and approved.
recommendations.citation: CY 2024 AAR, Part III, CY 2023 Observation No. 6, pp. 183-184

recommendations.recommendation: We recommended and Management agreed to: Ensure that approved climate change PPAs are aligned with the City’s LCCAP and funded from the City’s Internal Revenue Allotment (IRA) [now National Tax Allotment (NTA)] in accordance with Section 14 of RA No. 9729.
recommendations.status_note: Reiterated in Part II, Observation No. 26, Page 166
recommendations.management_action: -do-
recommendations.reason: As of the reporting date, no PPAs related to LCCAP have been submitted.
recommendations.citation: CY 2024 AAR, Part III, CY 2023 Observation No. 6, pp. 183-184

observations.summary: Seven hundred twenty-three (723) cases of double payment of emergency subsidy/financial assistance (FA) to beneficiaries in COVID-19 lockdown translated to a total payment of P8.424 million in excess of the amounts legally authorized.

recommendations.recommendation: We recommended that Management: Establish the accountability for and recover the excess payment of emergency subsidy and FA; and
recommendations.management_action: Management has sent letters/notices through registered mails (with registry receipts) to 308 Social Amelioration Program (SAP) beneficiaries
recommendations.reason: There has been no significant progress from Management on this matter.
recommendations.citation: CY 2024 AAR, Part III, CY 2021 Observation No. 4, pp. 184-185

recommendations.recommendation: We recommended that Management: In coordination with the DSWD, supply the missing beneficiary information necessary in the full validation of the payments of the subject emergency subsidy/FA.
recommendations.management_action: -do-
recommendations.citation: CY 2024 AAR, Part III, CY 2021 Observation No. 4, pp. 184-185

observations.summary: The City has not submitted 1,684 disbursement vouchers (DVs) and their supporting documents involving P2.275 billion, thereby limiting the extent of audit, preventing us to establish fully the validity of the underlying transactions, and forfeiting the benefit of, among others, timely detecting errors and deficiencies; identifying areas for improvement; and having input to assessments of accountability and decisions that need to be made. One thousand four hundred thirty-five (1,435) of these unsubmitted DVs in the amount of P2.142 billion pertain to the disbursements from CY 2015 to June 30, 2019 and are the accountabilities of the previous City Administrations.

recommendations.recommendation: We recommended that Management: Direct the CTO to: Produce and submit to the OCAT without further delay all the 288 DVs in Paragraph 1.7 of Observation No. 1;
recommendations.management_action: The OCAT in coordination with CTO is continuously remitting the remaining unremitted amount to date.
recommendations.reason: Records of CAO reveals that 1,188 DVs for the period 2015 to 2019 with a total amount of P2.026 billion remains unsubmitted.
recommendations.citation: CY 2024 AAR, Part III, CY 2019 Observation No. 1, pp. 185-187

recommendations.recommendation: We recommended that Management: Direct the CTO to: Submit to the OCAT within the prescribed period all the DVs supporting the Reports of Checks Issued (RCI); and
recommendations.management_action: -do-
recommendations.citation: CY 2024 AAR, Part III, CY 2019 Observation No. 1, pp. 185-187

recommendations.recommendation: Require the OCAT to: Submit to the City Auditor’s Office (CAO) without further delay all the 1,684 DVs specified in Paragraph 1.5 of Observation No. 1; and
recommendations.management_action: -do-
recommendations.citation: CY 2024 AAR, Part III, CY 2019 Observation No. 1, pp. 185-187

recommendations.recommendation: Require the OCAT to: Henceforth, submit to the CAO within the prescribed period all the DVs supporting the checks issued in the RCI with the list of original DVs still with the CTO, in the proper case, and stop the preparation of a separate schedule of DVs.
recommendations.management_action: -do-
recommendations.citation: CY 2024 AAR, Part III, CY 2019 Observation No. 1, pp. 185-187

observations.summary: The creation, organization and operation of an Internal Audit Service (IAS) mandated under Section 2 of RA No. 3456 as amended by RA No. 4177 was not undertaken by the City, thus, Management was not accorded with the assistance in the achievement of an efficient and effective fiscal administration and performance of agency affairs and functions. fair presentation of these accounts in the City’s FS.

recommendations.recommendation: We recommended that the Local Chief Executive (LCE) facilitate the creation, organization and operation of the City’s IAS as required under RA No. 3456 as amended by RA No. 4177, to assist in the achievement of an efficient and effective fiscal administration and performance of City’s affairs and functions.
recommendations.management_action: The City Council passed Ordinance No. 9093 creating the City Internal Audit Service on December 12, 2024.
recommendations.citation: CY 2024 AAR, Part III, CY 2018 Observation No. 15, pp. 187-188

observations.summary: The excess amount of collections/proceeds from sale of bid documents and other related fees amounting to P13.958 million as of December 31, 2018 was still being maintained under the trust fund (TF) instead of transferring the same to the general fund (GF) pursuant to Item 6.2 of Department of Budget and Management (DBM) Circular No. 2004-5A. Pursuant to Paragraph 10 of the Joint Venture Agreement JVA, we recommended that Management come up with JVA addendum/ amendments or similar binding document to correct the provisions and deficiencies therein that work against the interest of the City (Paragraphs 3.3, 3.10 and 3.11) with the end view of, among others:

recommendations.recommendation: We recommended that Management direct the City Treasurer to cause the immediate transfer of the unutilized amount of the proceeds from the collection of bid documents and related fees from the TF to the GF by the City.
recommendations.reason: The OCAT is still in the process of determining the excess collections/ proceeds. Once completed, a DV will be prepared for the fund transfer to the GF.
recommendations.citation: CY 2024 AAR, Part III, CY 2018 Observation No. 16, pp. 188-189
